subject: [neuprintR] depreciated support for older hemibrain databases?

messages.author: 1100dde5b99c8951
messages.subject: [neuprintR] depreciated support for older hemibrain databases?
parts:
Hello all,

Just wondering if anyone outside our lab has run into this issue: 

It appears that as of this week we cannot access the older (e.g. v1.01 and v1.1) databases on neuprint by editing the R environment file. Specifically, we are having issues downloading neurons/skeletons.

examples:
running: `neuprint_read_neurons(544021095)`
returns: `Error in neuprint_read_neurons(544021095) : Error reading bodyids`

and

running:` neuprint_read_skeletons(544021095)`
returns: ```Error: neuPrint error: <html>
<head><title>502 Bad Gateway</title></head>
<body bgcolor="white">
<center><h1>502 Bad Gateway</h1></center>
<hr><center>nginx/1.10.3</center>
</body>
</html>
```

When changing the R environment file to access V1.2 instead everything works fine. We are able to access V1.2, V1.1, V1.01 via the Python API just fine.

best,
Pasha

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] [neuprintR] depreciated support for older hemibrain databases?
parts:
Dear Pasha,

Many thanks for the report. What I saw was that accessing metadata for the older versions worked fine, but there was a specific problem with skeleton access. My test code is at the bottom of the email. However I also found that the skeletons could not be accessed via the neuprint website either. Are you sure the python client was working for the earlier datasets for skeletons? In any case, I queried with the neuprint devs and they actually found a misconfiguration that they fixed right away. All working now for me. Thanks again!

Greg.

c1=neuprint_login(dataset="hemibrain:v1.0.1", Force = T)
c2=neuprint_login(dataset="hemibrain:v1.1", Force = T)
c3=neuprint_login(dataset="hemibrain:v1.2", Force = T)

# all worked
neuprint_get_meta(544021095, conn=c1)
neuprint_get_meta(544021095, conn=c2)
neuprint_get_meta(544021095, conn=c3)

n1=neuprint_read_neurons(544021095, conn = c1)
n2=neuprint_read_neurons(544021095, conn = c2)
n3=neuprint_read_neurons(544021095, conn = c3)
